questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: The hypothalamus, which contains groups of neurosecretory cells that regulate the pituitary, is the basal part of the:

options.text: Diencephalon of the forebrain
Midbrain
Cerebellum of the hindbrain
Medulla oblongata

solution.explanation: NCERT describes the hypothalamus as the basal part of the diencephalon of the forebrain. It regulates a wide spectrum of body functions.
steps: Diencephalon is a part of the forebrain
solution.why_others_wrong: The midbrain, cerebellum and medulla are other parts of the brain; none of them contains the hypothalamus.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', The hypothalamus
solution.final_answer: Option A: Diencephalon of the forebrain

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: In females, besides causing a vigorous contraction of the uterus at the time of child birth, oxytocin stimulates:

options.text: Growth of the mammary glands and formation of milk
Milk ejection from the mammary glands
Formation of alveoli in the mammary glands
Resorption of water by the distal tubules of the kidney

solution.explanation: Oxytocin acts on the smooth muscles of the body. In females it stimulates a vigorous contraction of the uterus at child birth and milk ejection from the mammary glands.
steps: Second action in females: milk ejection
solution.why_others_wrong: Growth of the mammary glands and milk formation is the action of prolactin; formation of alveoli is stimulated by progesterone; water resorption by the distal tubules is the action of vasopressin.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', The pituitary gland
solution.final_answer: Option B: Milk ejection from the mammary glands

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: The hormones produced by the hypothalamus that regulate the pituitary are of two types. These are:

options.text: Glucocorticoids and mineralocorticoids
Estrogens and progestogens
Releasing hormones and inhibiting hormones
Iodothyronines and catecholamines

solution.explanation: NCERT: the hypothalamic hormones are of two types - releasing hormones, which stimulate the secretion of pituitary hormones, and inhibiting hormones, which inhibit it. GnRH is a releasing hormone; somatostatin is an inhibiting hormone.
solution.why_others_wrong: Glucocorticoids and mineralocorticoids come from the adrenal cortex, estrogens and progestogens from the ovary or placenta, and iodothyronines and catecholamines from the thyroid and adrenal medulla.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', The hypothalamus
solution.final_answer: Option C: Releasing hormones and inhibiting hormones

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Adrenaline and noradrenaline are rapidly secreted in response to stress of any kind and during emergency situations. They are therefore called:

options.text: Anti-diuretic hormones
Hypercalcemic hormones
Gonadotrophins
Emergency hormones or hormones of Fight or Flight

solution.explanation: NCERT calls adrenaline and noradrenaline emergency hormones or hormones of Fight or Flight, because they are rapidly secreted from the adrenal medulla in response to stress and emergencies.
steps: Released quickly in stress or emergency
Name: emergency hormones / hormones of Fight or Flight
solution.why_others_wrong: Anti-diuretic hormone is vasopressin, the hypercalcemic hormone is PTH, and gonadotrophins are LH and FSH.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', The adrenal gland

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: On the basis of their chemical nature, insulin, glucagon, the pituitary hormones and the hypothalamic hormones are all grouped as:

options.text: Peptide, polypeptide or protein hormones
Steroid hormones
Iodothyronines
Amino-acid derivatives

solution.explanation: NCERT groups hormones as (i) peptide, polypeptide and protein hormones (e.g., insulin, glucagon, pituitary hormones, hypothalamic hormones), (ii) steroids, (iii) iodothyronines and (iv) amino-acid derivatives.
steps: Insulin, glucagon, pituitary and hypothalamic hormones

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Aldosterone stimulates the excretion of K+ and phosphate ions by the renal tubules.
Statement II: The zona fasciculata forms the middle layer of the adrenal cortex.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Aldosterone acts mainly at the renal tubules, stimulating the reabsorption of Na+ and water and the excretion of K+ and phosphate ions. The adrenal cortex has three layers: zona reticularis (inner), zona fasciculata (middle) and zona glomerulosa (outer).
steps: Statement I: true (excretion of K+ and phosphate)
Statement II: true (fasciculata is the middle layer)
solution.why_others_wrong: Both statements are NCERT lines, so any option calling either of them false is wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', The adrenal gland
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Androgens produce anabolic (synthetic) effects on protein and carbohydrate metabolism.
Reason (R): Androgens are synthesised and secreted by the Leydig (interstitial) cells of the testis.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Both are NCERT statements. R tells us where androgens are made; it says nothing about why they have an anabolic effect on metabolism. Knowing the source of a hormone does not explain its effect on target tissues, so R is true but not the explanation of A.
steps: R gives the site of synthesis, which does not explain the metabolic effect
solution.why_others_wrong: A is wrong because R does not explain A; C and D are wrong because both statements are true.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', Testis
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

A. Estrogens
B. Androgens
C. Catecholamines
D. Thymosins

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Neural coordination is slow but long-lasting.
Statement II: Nerve fibres innervate every cell of the body, so hormones are not needed for the continuous regulation of cellular functions.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: the neural system provides point-to-point rapid coordination, which is fast but short-lived. As the nerve fibres do not innervate all cells of the body and cellular functions need continuous regulation, a special kind of coordination is provided by hormones.
steps: Statement I: false - neural coordination is fast but short-lived
Statement II: false - nerve fibres do not innervate all cells
solution.why_others_wrong: Statement I reverses NCERT's 'fast but short-lived' and Statement II contradicts the reason given for hormones, so every option calling either true is wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', Introduction (need for chemical coordination)
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.

questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Addison's disease is characterised by acute weakness and fatigue.
Reason (R): Addison's disease is caused by over-production of hormones by the adrenal cortex.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', The adrenal gland

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the pituitary gland are correct?

(a) LH and FSH are called gonadotrophins because they stimulate gonadal activity.
(b) The pars intermedia secretes only one hormone.
(c) If unchecked, acromegaly may lead to serious complications and premature death.
(d) ACTH stimulates the synthesis and secretion of mineralocorticoids from the adrenal cortex.
(e) In females, FSH maintains the corpus luteum.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: (a), (b), (c) and (e) only
(b), (d) and (e) only
(a), (b) and (c) only
(a) and (d) only

solution.explanation: LH and FSH stimulate gonadal activity and are therefore called gonadotrophins. The pars intermedia secretes only one hormone, MSH. Acromegaly, if unchecked, may lead to serious complications and premature death. ACTH stimulates the secretion of glucocorticoids (not mineralocorticoids), and it is LH (not FSH) that maintains the corpus luteum.
steps: (e) False: LH maintains the corpus luteum
solution.why_others_wrong: Every other option includes (d) or (e), which swap glucocorticoids with mineralocorticoids and LH with FSH.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', The pituitary gland
solution.final_answer: Option C: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the pancreas and blood glucose are correct?

(a) The pancreas acts as both an exocrine and an endocrine gland.
(b) Glucagon reduces the cellular glucose uptake and utilisation.
(c) Glucagon stimulates gluconeogenesis, which also contributes to hyperglycemia.
(d) Insulin and glucagon are steroid hormones.
(e) Glucose homeostasis in blood is maintained by insulin alone.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: (a), (b), (c) and (e) only
(b), (c) and (d) only
(a), (d) and (e) only
(a), (b) and (c) only

solution.explanation: The pancreas is a composite gland, acting as both an exocrine and an endocrine gland. Glucagon reduces cellular glucose uptake and utilisation, stimulates glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis, and is hyperglycemic. Insulin and glucagon are peptide hormones, and glucose homeostasis is maintained jointly by the two.
steps: (e) False: maintained jointly by insulin and glucagon
solution.why_others_wrong: (d) and (e) are false, and every other option contains at least one of them.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', Pancreas
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: A drug blocks the generation of second messengers (such as cyclic AMP, IP3 and Ca2+) in target cells, but does not affect intracellular receptors. The action of which of the following hormones is most likely to be blocked?

options.text: Cortisol
Glucagon
Thyroxine
Testosterone

solution.explanation: Hormones that bind membrane-bound receptors do not enter the cell; they generate second messengers. Hormones that bind intracellular receptors (steroids, iodothyronines) regulate gene expression directly. Glucagon is a peptide hormone, so it acts through membrane receptors and second messengers; cortisol and testosterone (steroids) and thyroxine (an iodothyronine) act through intracellular receptors.
steps: Blocking second messengers affects membrane-receptor hormones
Steroids and iodothyronines use intracellular receptors
Glucagon (peptide) is the only membrane-receptor hormone listed
solution.why_others_wrong: Cortisol and testosterone are steroids and thyroxine is an iodothyronine; NCERT says these interact with intracellular receptors, which the drug does not affect.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', Mechanism of hormone action
solution.final_answer: Option B: Glucagon

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: In a patient, the adrenal cortex has stopped secreting its hormones but the adrenal medulla works normally. Which of the following would still be secreted normally by the adrenal gland?

options.text: Cortisol
Aldosterone
Adrenaline and noradrenaline
Small amounts of androgenic steroids that support pubic and axial hair growth

solution.concept: Products of the adrenal cortex and medulla
solution.explanation: The adrenal medulla secretes adrenaline and noradrenaline (catecholamines). The adrenal cortex secretes the corticoids - glucocorticoids such as cortisol, mineralocorticoids such as aldosterone - and small amounts of androgenic steroids. With the cortex failing, only the medullary hormones remain normal.
solution.why_others_wrong: Cortisol, aldosterone and the adrenal androgenic steroids are all products of the adrenal cortex, which has failed in this patient.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', The adrenal gland
solution.final_answer: Option C: Adrenaline and noradrenaline

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the gonads and their hormones are correct?

(a) The ovary produces one ovum during each menstrual cycle.
(b) Androgens regulate the development, maturation and functions of the prostate gland and urethra.
(c) Estrogens are secreted mainly by the corpus luteum.
(d) Estrogens stimulate mammary gland development.
(e) Progesterone is a peptide hormone.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: (a), (c) and (d) only
(b), (d) and (e) only
(a), (b), (c) and (d) only
(a), (b) and (d) only

solution.concept: Hormones of the testis and ovary
solution.explanation: The ovary produces one ovum during each menstrual cycle. Androgens regulate the male accessory sex organs, including the prostate gland and urethra. Estrogens are secreted mainly by the growing ovarian follicles and stimulate mammary gland development; the corpus luteum secretes mainly progesterone. Progesterone, like estrogen, is a steroid hormone.
solution.why_others_wrong: (c) gives estrogen the corpus luteum as its main source and (e) calls progesterone a peptide; every other option includes one of them.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', Testis; Ovary
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (b) and (d) only

questions.question_text: The process of delivery of the foetus (child birth) at the end of pregnancy is called:

options.text: Implantation
Parturition
Insemination
Ovulation

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: In the human mammary gland, the alveoli open into the:

options.text: Lactiferous duct directly
Mammary ampulla directly
Mammary tubules
Fallopian tubes

solution.concept: Duct system of the mammary gland
solution.explanation: NCERT: the cells of the alveoli secrete milk, which is stored in their cavities. The alveoli open into mammary tubules; the tubules of each lobe join to form a mammary duct.
steps: Tubules of each lobe -> mammary duct
solution.why_others_wrong: The ampulla and lactiferous duct come later in the path (mammary ducts -> ampulla -> lactiferous duct); fallopian tubes belong to the reproductive tract, not the breast.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', The female reproductive system

questions.question_text: Each human ovary is covered by a thin epithelium which encloses the:

options.text: Endometrium
Myometrium
Seminiferous tubules
Ovarian stroma

solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', The female reproductive system
solution.final_answer: Option D: Ovarian stroma

Glands: seminal vesicles, prostate, bulbourethral glands
solution.why_others_wrong: The second option lists accessory glands, the third lists parts and cells of the testis, and the fourth lists urinary passages.

options.text: Spermiation
Ovulation
Menarche

steps: R describes women, so it does not explain A

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: In a human male, a primary spermatocyte has 46 chromosomes (44 autosomes + X + Y). It completes meiosis normally and the four spermatids become sperms. How many of these sperms carry a Y chromosome, and how many autosomes does each sperm contain?

options.text: 1 sperm carries Y; each sperm has 22 autosomes
2 sperms carry Y; each sperm has 44 autosomes
2 sperms carry Y; each sperm has 22 autosomes
4 sperms carry Y; each sperm has 23 autosomes

solution.concept: Meiosis and sex chromosomes in sperms
solution.explanation: Meiosis halves the chromosome number: each sperm gets 22 autosomes plus one sex chromosome. The X and Y separate in meiosis, so of the four sperms formed from one primary spermatocyte, two carry X and two carry Y. This is why about 50 per cent of sperms carry X and 50 per cent carry Y.
steps: Sex chromosomes: X and Y separate; 4 sperms -> 2 X + 2 Y
solution.why_others_wrong: '1 sperm' ignores that the two secondary spermatocytes each divide again; 44 autosomes forgets the halving in meiosis; 23 counts the sex chromosome as an autosome and '4 Y' ignores X-Y segregation.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Gametogenesis; Fertilisation and implantation
solution.final_answer: Option C: 2 sperms carry Y; each sperm has 22 autosomes

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: During the luteal phase, the endometrium is maintained by progesterone from the corpus luteum. According to NCERT, such an endometrium is necessary for:

options.text: Implantation of the fertilised ovum and other events of pregnancy
Rupture of the Graafian follicle
Transport of sperms to the ampulla
Formation of the zona pellucida

questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The vasa efferentia open directly into the vas deferens.
Statement II: The female reproductive system is located in the pelvic region.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Male duct path and female system location
solution.explanation: The seminiferous tubules open into the vasa efferentia through the rete testis; the vasa efferentia leave the testis and open into the epididymis, which leads to the vas deferens. Gradual descent from common ancestors is evolution, not special creation

solution.concept: Working back from genotype frequencies to allele frequencies
solution.explanation: p² + 2pq + q² = 1, so 2pq = 1 - 0.58 = 0.42 and pq = 0.21. With p + q = 1, p and q are the roots of x(1 - x) = 0.21, i.e., 0.7 and 0.3. Check: 0.7² + 0.3² = 0.49 + 0.09 = 0.58. The more common allele has frequency 0.7.
solution.why_others_wrong: 0.42 is the heterozygote frequency (2pq), 0.21 is pq, and 0.58 is the given homozygote total; none is an allele frequency.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 6 'Evolution', Hardy-Weinberg principle
solution.final_answer: Option A: 0.7

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: In a population of 500 people, the alleles M and N of a gene are codominant. The population has 180 MM, 240 MN and 80 NN individuals. What is the frequency of allele M, and is the population in Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium?

options.text: 0.6; no, there is an excess of heterozygotes
0.36; yes, it is in Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium
0.48; no, there is a deficit of heterozygotes
0.6; yes, it is in Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium

solution.explanation: With codominance every genotype can be counted. Allele M = (2 x 180 + 240) / (2 x 500) = 600 / 1000 = 0.6, so N = 0.4. Expected numbers at equilibrium: MM = 0.36 x 500 = 180, MN = 2 x 0.6 x 0.4 x 500 = 240, NN = 0.16 x 500 = 80. Observed equals expected, so the population is in Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium.
solution.why_others_wrong: 0.36 is the MM genotype frequency and 0.48 the MN frequency, not the allele frequency; the observed MN count (240) equals the expected count, so there is neither an excess nor a deficit of heterozygotes.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 6 'Evolution', Hardy-Weinberg principle
solution.final_answer: Option D: 0.6; yes, it is in Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Restriction endonucleases recognise palindromic sequences, which read the same on the two strands of DNA when the orientation of reading is kept the same (5' to 3'). Which of the following double-stranded sequences, given as its upper (5' to 3') strand, is a palindrome?

options.text: 5'-GGATCC-3'
5'-GATCTC-3'
5'-AAGCTA-3'
5'-GGAACC-3'

solution.explanation: A sequence is palindromic if its complementary strand, read 5' to 3', is the same. For 5'-GGATCC-3' the complementary strand is 3'-CCTAGG-5', which read 5' to 3' is GGATCC - identical. The other sequences give different sequences when the complementary strand is read 5' to 3'.
solution.shortcut: The second half must be the complement of the first half read backwards: GGA|TCC.
solution.why_others_wrong: GATCTC reads GAGATC on the other strand, AAGCTA reads TAGCTT and GGAACC reads GGTTCC; none is the same on both strands.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Tools of recombinant DNA technology (restriction enzymes)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: A PCR starts with a single double-stranded DNA molecule. Every new DNA strand is synthesised by extension of one primer, and each cycle copies every strand present. After 3 cycles, how many primer molecules have been incorporated into DNA?

solution.explanation: After n cycles there are 2^n double-stranded molecules, i.e., 2^(n+1) strands. Only the 2 original template strands were not made by extending a primer; every other strand begins with one primer. For n = 3: 2^4 = 16 strands, so 16 - 2 = 14 primers are incorporated.
solution.why_others_wrong: 8 counts double-stranded molecules, 16 counts all strands including the two original template strands, and 6 assumes only two primers per cycle.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Amplification of gene of interest using PCR
